:::note[External requirement set]

This is not one of the Dutch scheme documents. It is a requirement set published by the OWASP Mobile Application Security (MAS) project, which the Dutch cybersecurity certification scheme uses. Texts © OWASP Foundation, licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Source: [OWASP MAS-EUDIW](https://mas.owasp.org/Profiles/MAS-EUDIW/).

:::

## How the Dutch scheme uses it {#use}

[NL-CS Part 1](/edi-stelsel-certification/documents/nl-cs-part-1) section 4.4 says that "the required test set is built on OWASP MAS". The scheme references OWASP MAS material and does not reproduce it; the evaluation plan pins the version of every OWASP deliverable used and records its draft status where applicable ([NL-CS Part 1 §4.4, p. 14](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-CS-part1-RC1.0_EUDIW_-_for_publ.pdf#page=14)). The section lists:

- OWASP MASVS v2.1.0, whose categories structure the required test set;
- OWASP MASWE v1.0: required tests and the test-to-requirement mapping are identified by MASWE identifier;
- OWASP MASTG for the test procedures, in the version current when the evaluation plan is issued;
- the OWASP MAS testing profiles. The baseline combination for the wallet at assurance level high is L2 + R + P, marked "[FOR REVIEW]";
- the **OWASP MAS EUDI Wallet profile (W)**, "applied on top". NL-CS Part 1 describes it as "Draft as at the date of this version and not yet normative".

The same test set is referred to for penetration testing (EN 17640 task 6.10) in [NL-CS Part 2 §4.3](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-cs-part-2#s-4-3) ([p. 14](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-CS-part2-RC1.0_-_for_publ.pdf#page=14)), and in the evaluation instruction [NL-CS Part 3 §4.7](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-cs-part-3#s-4-7) ([p. 11](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-CS-part3-RC1.0_-_for_publ.pdf#page=11)). The draft protection profile's mapping of each FSR and RSR to OWASP MAS shall be re-keyed to MASWE v1.0 identifiers before issue ([NL-CS Part 1 §4.3, p. 13](pathname:///files/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/NL-CS-part1-RC1.0_EUDIW_-_for_publ.pdf#page=13)).

:::caution[Different numbering in NL-CS-WI]

[NL-CS-WI Annex C](/edi-stelsel-certification/text/nl-cs-wi#s-c) maps the Wallet Instance requirements to "OWASP Requirements" with an earlier numbering and wording. For example, its "#9 - The app rotates cryptographic keys regularly" is [#15](#r15) in version v1.0 below. The numbers in Annex C do not refer to this list.

:::

## About this version {#version}

- **Catalogue:** EUDI Wallet MAS Profile – Security Requirements, version v1.0, status Final, last updated 15.09.2026.
- **Authors:** Carlos Holguera, Jeroen Beckers, Sven Schleier. **Reviewers:** Erik van Zuuren, Chris DeVuyst, Petteri Ihalainen.
- **Requirements:** 78. Requirement #75 is marked "OUT OF SCOPE for the OWASP MAS EUDIW Profile"; the [OWASP web page](https://mas.owasp.org/Profiles/MAS-EUDIW/) lists the other 77, with the same texts.
- Each requirement is mapped to an OWASP MASWE weakness and MASVS category, and to the threats (TR), technical threats (TT) and risks (R) of the risk register for European Digital Identity Wallets.
- **Official downloads:** [Requirements Catalogue](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VQrZSr0ErR0RH1tl4QS42_K27sZH8Cad678l0BB3sFs/) (spreadsheet) and [Practical Guidelines](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cXAYSe6MsWJ03tiCmlwV_k8Rb30w6rdW/view) (PDF), both linked from the [OWASP MAS-EUDIW page](https://mas.owasp.org/Profiles/MAS-EUDIW/).
- All 78 requirements are also in the [requirement search](/edi-stelsel-certification/requirements) and the [requirement data sets](/edi-stelsel-certification/downloads#data).

## MASVS-STORAGE {#masvs-storage}

### \#1 — The app encrypts sensitive data stored in private storage. {#r1}

**MASWE:** [MASWE-0001: Sensitive Data Stored Unencrypted in Private Storage](https://mas.owasp.org/MASWE/MASVS-STORAGE/MASWE-0001/)

- **Threats:** TR0x05 - An attacker can abuse the cryptographic implementation of the solution, TR0x08 - An attacker can modify the app during runtime
- **Technical threats:** TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.2 Information leakage, TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.1 Theft, TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.3 Tampering
- **Risks:** R4 - Identify theft, R6 - Data disclosure, R5 - Data theft, R7 - Data manipulation, R8 - Data loss
- **Example assets:** [PIN Salt](#as19), [PIN Public Key](#as20), [Wallet Configuration](#as35), [Person Identification Data (PID)](#as1), [Access Certificates (Providers & Relying Parties)](#as27), [PIN Private Key](#as15), [Attestations ((Q)EAA / PuB-EAA)](#as2), [User PII (other collected data)](#as9)
- **Baseline configurations:** [platform-provided secure keystore](#cf07), [approved cryptographic algorithms](#cf10)

### \#2 — The app encrypts sensitive data stored outside of private storage. {#r2}

**MASWE:** [MASWE-0002: Sensitive Data Stored Unencrypted Outside of Private Storage](https://mas.owasp.org/MASWE/MASVS-STORAGE/MASWE-0002/)

- **Technical threats:** TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.1 Theft, TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.2 Information leakage, TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.3 Tampering
- **Risks:** R4 - Identify theft, R6 - Data disclosure, R5 - Data theft, R7 - Data manipulation, R8 - Data loss
- **Example assets:** [PIN Salt](#as19), [PIN Public Key](#as20), [Wallet Configuration](#as35), [Person Identification Data (PID)](#as1), [Access Certificates (Providers & Relying Parties)](#as27), [PIN Private Key](#as15), [Attestations ((Q)EAA / PuB-EAA)](#as2), [User PII (other collected data)](#as9)
- **Baseline configurations:** [platform-provided secure keystore](#cf07), [approved cryptographic algorithms](#cf10)

### \#3 — The app stores cryptographic keys inside the platform-provided secure keystore. {#r3}

**MASWE:** [MASWE-0003: Cryptographic Keys Stored Outside of Platform Keystore](https://mas.owasp.org/MASWE/MASVS-STORAGE/MASWE-0003/)

- **Threats:** TR0x05 - An attacker can abuse the cryptographic implementation of the solution
- **Technical threats:** TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.2 Information leakage, TT2 - Errors and misconfigurations - 2.3 Development-time errors and system misconfigurations
- **Risks:** R6 - Data disclosure, R7 - Data manipulation
- **Example assets:** [Non-critical Cryptographic Keys](#as11), [Configuration Public Key](#as23), [PIN Private Key](#as15)
- **Baseline configurations:** [platform-provided secure keystore](#cf07)

### \#4 — The app does not hardcode sensitive data in the application package. {#r4}

**MASWE:** [MASWE-0004: Sensitive Data Hardcoded in the App Package](https://mas.owasp.org/MASWE/MASVS-STORAGE/MASWE-0004/)

- **Threats:** TR0x05 - An attacker can abuse the cryptographic implementation of the solution, TR0x10 - An attacker can extract hardcoded sensitive data from the app package.
- **Technical threats:** TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.2 Information leakage, TT2 - Errors and misconfigurations - 2.3 Development-time errors and system misconfigurations
- **Risks:** R6 - Data disclosure
- **Example assets:** [Critical Private Keys (PID / attestation proof keys)](#as10), [Authorization Codes and Access Tokens](#as33), [Access Certificates (Providers & Relying Parties)](#as27)

### \#5 — The app excludes sensitive data from application logs. {#r5}

**MASWE:** [MASWE-0005: Insertion of Sensitive Data into Logs](https://mas.owasp.org/MASWE/MASVS-STORAGE/MASWE-0005/)

- **Threats:** TR33 - An attacker can extract logs or parts of them.
- **Technical threats:** TT1 - Physical attacks - 1.2 Information leakage, TT2 - Errors and misconfigurations - 2.3 Development-time errors and system misconfigurations
- **Risks:** R6 - Data disclosure
- **Example assets:** [Runtime / Crash Logs](#as39), [Transaction / Usage Logs](#as38)

### \#6 — The app excludes sensitive data from backups. {#r6}

**MASWE:** [MASWE-0006: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup](https://mas.owasp.org/MASWE/MASVS-STORAGE/MASWE-0006/)

- **Threats:** TR48 - An attacker can modify the content of backup and recovery data that should be exclusively under the user's control., TR54 - An attacker can read the content of backup and recovery data that should be exclusively under the user's control.

## Assets {#assets}

The assets the requirements refer to, as defined in the catalogue. It is up to the user of the profile to map the relevant assets to the requirements.

### AS1 — Person Identification Data (PID) {#as1}

Core set of identity attributes issued to the user at Level of Assurance High by a PID Provider, including the issuer signature.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7), [\#19](#r19), [\#30](#r30), [\#36](#r36), [\#37](#r37), [\#38](#r38), [\#39](#r39), [\#40](#r40)

### AS2 — Attestations ((Q)EAA / PuB-EAA) {#as2}

Electronic attestations of attributes (qualified, public-sector or non-qualified), e.g. driving licences or diplomas; attributes plus issuer signature, selectively disclosable.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7)

### AS3 — Wallet Unit Attestation (WUA) {#as3}

A signed object attesting to the hardware security properties and component compliance of the Wallet Unit; the WUA private key never resides in the app (signed by the Wallet Provider backend); decrypted only when needed, re-encrypted immediately after.

**Used by:** –

### AS4 — Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) {#as4}

A signed object asserting the integrity and genuineness of the installed mobile application (Wallet Instance); revocable via Token Status List.

**Used by:** [\#11](#r11), [\#56](#r56)

### AS5 — Pseudonyms and Passkeys {#as5}

User-chosen or issuer-provided identifiers (incl. FIDO2/passkey material) for pseudonymous authentication towards Relying Parties without enabling tracking.

**Used by:** [\#19](#r19), [\#67](#r67), [\#68](#r68), [\#69](#r69)

### AS6 — Embedded Disclosure Policy {#as6}

A set of rules embedded in an attestation by its provider defining which Relying Parties are authorized to receive it; evaluated by the wallet before presentation.

**Used by:** [\#69](#r69), [\#71](#r71)

### AS7 — Transactional Data {#as7}

Specific data points (e.g. payment amount, payee) contained in a presentation request that must be shown to and approved by the User.

**Used by:** [\#23](#r23), [\#32](#r32), [\#37](#r37), [\#38](#r38), [\#70](#r70)

### AS8 — Migration Object {#as8}

A list of the current PIDs and attestations (explicitly excluding private keys) used to restore the wallet content on a new device.

**Used by:** [\#6](#r6)

### AS9 — User PII (other collected data) {#as9}

Personally identifiable information collected by the app outside PID/attestations (e.g. e-mail, device identifiers) as declared in the privacy manifest.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7), [\#30](#r30), [\#36](#r36), [\#37](#r37), [\#66](#r66), [\#67](#r67), [\#71](#r71), [\#72](#r72), [\#73](#r73), [\#74](#r74), [\#76](#r76), [\#77](#r77)

### AS10 — Critical Private Keys (PID / attestation proof keys) {#as10}

Private keys bound to PID and other device-bound attestations, used to sign proofs of possession during presentation; managed exclusively by the WSCA/WSCD (in remote-HSM architectures they never reach the app).

**Used by:** [\#4](#r4), [\#10](#r10), [\#13](#r13), [\#16](#r16), [\#22](#r22), [\#33](#r33)

### AS11 — Non-critical Cryptographic Keys {#as11}

Keys used for less sensitive attestations and operations that do not require Level of Assurance High protection.

**Used by:** [\#3](#r3), [\#13](#r13), [\#15](#r15)

### AS12 — Hardware-Bound Private Key {#as12}

A unique, non-exportable device key used to sign instructions sent to the backend, serving as the possession factor of user authentication.

**Used by:** [\#10](#r10), [\#16](#r16), [\#22](#r22), [\#25](#r25)

### AS13 — Wallet Key Encryption Key (KEK) {#as13}

A hardware-bound key used exclusively to wrap (encrypt) the local database encryption key; never leaves the secure hardware.

**Used by:** [\#16](#r16)

### AS14 — Database Encryption Key & IV {#as14}

The AES-256 key and Initialization Vector required to unlock the local encrypted (SQLCipher) database; stored on mobile storage only in wrapped form, decryptable solely via the KEK inside the SE/TEE.

**Used by:** [\#16](#r16)

### AS15 — PIN Private Key {#as15}

A P-256 private key derived on-the-fly from PIN + PIN Salt for a specific instruction and discarded immediately after use; never persisted.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#3](#r3), [\#7](#r7), [\#10](#r10), [\#14](#r14), [\#20](#r20), [\#24](#r24)

### AS16 — WSCA Secure-Channel Keys {#as16}

Credentials/keys used by the Wallet Instance to establish the mutually authenticated secure channel to the WSCA; compromise enables full identity takeover.

**Used by:** –

### AS17 — TLS / Secure-Channel Session Keys {#as17}

Ephemeral session keys protecting network communication (TLS 1.3) and application-level payload encryption between app, backend and counterparties.

**Used by:** [\#15](#r15), [\#62](#r62)

### AS18 — Random Numbers (CSPRNG output) {#as18}

Cryptographically secure random values used for key derivation, IVs, nonces, challenges and tokens.

**Used by:** [\#12](#r12)

### AS19 — PIN Salt {#as19}

32 random bytes used as input for the on-the-fly derivation of the PIN private key; never stored together with the PIN itself.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7), [\#12](#r12), [\#14](#r14)

### AS20 — PIN Public Key {#as20}

The public counterpart of the PIN private key, used by the backend to verify the user knowledge factor; sent to the backend during enrollment - the wallet retains only an HMAC of this key inside its WB Certificate.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7)

### AS21 — Hardware Public Key {#as21}

The public counterpart of the hardware-bound device key, used by the backend to verify instruction signatures.

**Used by:** –

### AS22 — Infrastructure Public Keys {#as22}

Public keys (e.g. WB Response Signing Public Key, WUA Signing public key) used by the app to verify signed data coming from the backend; contained within the Wallet Configuration.

**Used by:** –

### AS23 — Configuration Public Key {#as23}

The pinned key used by the application to verify the digital signature of the Wallet Configuration JWT (root of the configuration trust chain), preventing a malicious server from supplying false settings.

**Used by:** [\#3](#r3)

### AS24 — Wallet Backend (WB) Certificate {#as24}

A WB-signed JWT binding the wallet identity and its public keys (incl. HMAC of the PIN public key); issued during enrollment and presented with every backend instruction.

**Used by:** –

### AS25 — Trust Anchors and CA Certificates {#as25}

Self-signed certificates and trust anchors (from the EU Trusted Lists) used to authenticate the backend, PID/attestation issuers and Relying Parties, incl. identity-pinning material; contained within the Wallet Configuration.

**Used by:** [\#11](#r11), [\#27](#r27), [\#28](#r28)

### AS26 — Intermediate Signing Certificates {#as26}

Certificates in the chain between a Trust Anchor and the final entity certificate, validated during chain verification.

**Used by:** –

### AS27 — Access Certificates (Providers & Relying Parties) {#as27}

Certificates issued to PID Providers, Attestation Providers and Relying Parties, presented to the wallet during transactions to authenticate the counterparty.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#4](#r4), [\#7](#r7), [\#11](#r11)

### AS28 — Registration Certificates {#as28}

Certificates detailing the specific data types an entity (issuer or Relying Party) is registered and authorized to request or issue.

**Used by:** –

### AS29 — Qualified Certificates (PuB-EAA / QSeal) {#as29}

Qualified certificates used by public sector bodies and QTSPs to sign attestations; validated by the wallet as part of PuB-EAA verification.

**Used by:** –

### AS30 — Revocation & Status Data (Status Lists, CRLs) {#as30}

Attestation/Certificate revocation and status information (e.g. Token Status Lists, Attestation Status Lists, CRLs) fetched to check validity of attestations, WIAs and certificates.

**Used by:** –

### AS31 — PIN {#as31}

The knowledge factor for user authentication and authorization of sensitive transactions; entered by the user per transaction and used only for on-the-fly derivation of the PIN private key.

**Used by:** [\#20](#r20), [\#21](#r21), [\#23](#r23), [\#33](#r33), [\#36](#r36), [\#38](#r38), [\#39](#r39), [\#40](#r40)

### AS32 — Biometric Data / Templates {#as32}

Fingerprint, face or iris templates referenced for the inherence factor; managed entirely by the platform biometric API and never accessible to the app.

**Used by:** [\#20](#r20), [\#21](#r21), [\#23](#r23)

### AS33 — Authorization Codes and Access Tokens {#as33}

Short-lived OAuth2/OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP protocol tokens used during issuance and presentation of credentials.

**Used by:** [\#4](#r4), [\#29](#r29), [\#32](#r32)

### AS34 — User Session State {#as34}

Session context of an authenticated wallet user (unlock state, timeouts, retry counters); must be invalidated on termination and contextual state changes.

**Used by:** [\#24](#r24)

### AS35 — Wallet Configuration {#as35}

A signed JWT containing service URLs, trust anchors for certificate pinning, and version-pinning information; periodically fetched from the backend and signature-verified by the app.

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7)

### AS36 — Configuration URL {#as36}

The permanent bootstrap address where the app fetches the latest Wallet Configuration.

**Used by:** –

### AS37 — Service URLs {#as37}

Official URLs of the Wallet Backend, PID issuer and other relevant services, delivered inside the signed Wallet Configuration.

**Used by:** –

### AS38 — Transaction / Usage Logs {#as38}

The local record of all issuance and disclosure events performed by the Wallet Unit (presentation requests, Relying Party identities, presented attributes, timestamps), viewable by the user.

**Used by:** [\#5](#r5)

### AS39 — Runtime / Crash Logs {#as39}

Diagnostics sent to the Wallet Provider backend for maintenance (uncaught runtime errors, UX/telemetry data).

**Used by:** [\#5](#r5)

### AS40 — User Consent Records {#as40}

Records of explicit, informed user consent for data collection, processing and sharing (GDPR compliance artifacts).

**Used by:** [\#25](#r25), [\#70](#r70), [\#78](#r78)

### AS41 — Other Backup Data {#as41}

Device or cloud backup archives that could include app data; sensitive wallet data must be excluded or encrypted.

**Used by:** [\#6](#r6)

### AS42 — Network Traffic {#as42}

All data transmitted between the app and backend/issuers/Relying Parties.

**Used by:** [\#26](#r26), [\#27](#r27), [\#28](#r28), [\#62](#r62)

### AS43 — Wallet App Code & Resources {#as43}

The application binary, resources and packaged assets whose integrity the app must verify (anti-tampering, obfuscation, no debug artifacts or hardcoded secrets).

**Used by:** [\#34](#r34), [\#48](#r48), [\#49](#r49), [\#57](#r57), [\#58](#r58), [\#59](#r59), [\#60](#r60), [\#61](#r61)

### AS44 — Third-Party Libraries {#as44}

External SDKs, frameworks and open-source dependencies bundled with the app; regularly scanned for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and deprecated APIs.

**Used by:** [\#44](#r44), [\#46](#r46), [\#48](#r48)

### AS45 — Attestation Private Keys {#as45}

The actual private keys used to sign proofs of possession during disclosure; managed remotely within an HSM and never reach the mobile device.

**Used by:** –

### AS46 — Attestation Wrapping Key {#as46}

Master AES-256-GCM key used to encrypt all attestation private keys stored in the WB database; never leaves the HSM.

**Used by:** –

### AS47 — Infrastructure Private Keys {#as47}

Dedicated backend keys for signing WB certificates, instruction responses and Wallet Unit Attestations (incl. PIN Public Key Encryption/HMAC keys).

**Used by:** –

### AS48 — Key Attestation {#as48}

A type of Wallet Unit Attestation that attests the certification and properties of a WSCA/WSCD or keystore available to the Wallet Unit, and that contains one or more public keys whose corresponding private keys are generated by and stored in that WSCA/WSCD or keystore, as well as a revocation reference for the WSCD or keystore.

**Used by:** [\#11](#r11), [\#54](#r54)

## Baseline configurations {#baseline-configurations}

The configuration values the requirements refer to. The catalogue gives example values; the applicable values are set by the user of the profile.

### CF01 — outdated app version {#cf01}

The minimum App version allowed to run.

**Example value:** 8.3

**Used by:** [\#43](#r43)

### CF02 — minimum OS version {#cf02}

The minimum OS the application is allowed to run on.

**Example value:** 13.0

**Used by:** [\#41](#r41)

### CF03 — secure key generation {#cf03}

A list of algorithms and minimum key lengths.

**Example value:** RSA-2048 / AES-256

**Used by:** [\#13](#r13)

### CF04 — encrypted network traffic {#cf04}

A list of accepted network-encryption protocols.

**Example value:** TLS 1.3 minimum

**Used by:** [\#26](#r26), [\#27](#r27), [\#28](#r28), [\#62](#r62)

### CF05 — latest platform version {#cf05}

The platform version against which the app is built.

**Example value:** API 37

**Used by:** [\#42](#r42)

### CF06 — user collected/shared data {#cf06}

A list of approved collected data categories and types.

**Example value:** Precise location, User ID, Address

**Used by:** [\#66](#r66), [\#71](#r71), [\#73](#r73), [\#76](#r76), [\#77](#r77)

### CF07 — platform-provided secure keystore {#cf07}

The minimum requirement for hardware-backed keystores.

**Example value:** StrongBox / Secure Enclave

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#3](#r3), [\#20](#r20)

### CF08 — key rotation {#cf08}

A list of approved key lifetimes and usage counts.

**Example value:** defined per key class

**Used by:** [\#15](#r15)

### CF09 — key access restriction {#cf09}

A list of minimum key access restrictions.

**Example value:** non-exportable

**Used by:** [\#16](#r16)

### CF10 — approved cryptographic algorithms {#cf10}

A list of approved cryptographic algorithms.

**Example value:** SOG-IS ACM

**Used by:** [\#1](#r1), [\#2](#r2), [\#7](#r7), [\#8](#r8), [\#9](#r9), [\#10](#r10), [\#11](#r11), [\#12](#r12), [\#14](#r14)

### CF11 — allowed tracking domain {#cf11}

A list of approved tracking domains.

**Example value:** none

**Used by:** [\#68](#r68), [\#74](#r74)

### CF12 — device integrity state {#cf12}

A list of detection mechanisms to evaulate the trusted state of the device.

**Example value:** not rooted/jailbroken, no emulator/virtualization, secure lock screen configured).

**Used by:** [\#17](#r17), [\#41](#r41), [\#51](#r51), [\#52](#r52), [\#53](#r53), [\#54](#r54), [\#55](#r55)

### CF13 — app integrity state {#cf13}

A list of detection mechanisms to evaulate the trusted state of the running application.

**Example value:** the installed binary is genuine and unmodified (matches the signed release), not repackaged or tampered with, running in release mode, and not being debugged, instrumented, or hooked at runtime. Verified via runtime integrity checks and app attestation (e.g. Play Integrity / App Attest), and asserted towards the backend through the Wallet Instance Attestation.

**Used by:** [\#55](#r55), [\#56](#r56), [\#57](#r57), [\#58](#r58), [\#64](#r64), [\#65](#r65)

### CF14 — maximum failed authentication attempts {#cf14}

The number of consecutive failed local authentication attempts (PIN/biometric) permitted before the wallet instance is deactivated or protective action is taken on the retry counter.

**Example value:** 5.0

**Used by:** [\#20](#r20), [\#21](#r21), [\#23](#r23)
